task.description: Produce the design artefact for REQ-023 (event-store schema/migrations) at lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md, per WF-02 Step 1. Design only -- no implementation code, no .ex/.exs files, no migration files. Cover all six tables REQ-023 names (events, instance_sequence, event_payload_store, events_archive, the idempotency sidecar, instance_projections), each with full column/type/constraint/index detail, the Ecto.Schema module shape, and the migration shape using Ecto's :prefix option per REQ-022's already-shipped schema-per-tenant mechanism. Read docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md IN FULL before starting (REQ-023's own text says so) and cite Decision C's numbered points where the design follows them. Cross-check every table against R-Co's own src/design/event_store.md (ES-01..ES-08) rather than inventing a shape. State open questions explicitly instead of silently resolving them.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains migrations for events, instance_sequence, event_payload_store, events_archive, the idempotency sidecar table, and instance_projections, all using Ecto's :prefix option and applying cleanly against at least one provisioned tenant schema via REQ-022's migration-replay mechanism
events' migration defines the primary key as (event_id, created_at), not a bare event_id, per 0003 Decision C point 2(a)

the events Ecto.Schema module has no update_changeset/2 or any function that issues an UPDATE against a committed row; the moduledoc states this is a deliberate immutability invariant per 0003 Decision C point 1
the idempotency sidecar table has a unique index on idempotency_key and its own moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md's Open Question #1 two-phase-check recommendation per 0003's resolution
instance_projections' moduledoc explicitly states its schema is event-store scope (this requirement) while its meaningful population is EE-01/S3 scope, not built here

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md (11 sections, design-only -- no function bodies, no .ex/.exs files, no migration files). Sources read in full and cited by file:line throughout: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-023 (898-974) plus the S2 batch header (795-840) and REQ-022/024/025/026; docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md IN FULL (Decision A 29-35, B 37-45, C 46-59, Dimension C's point 1 at 254-262, point 2(a) at 273-277, point 2(b) at 277-282, point 3 at 284-294, closing tenant paragraph 296-309); docs/migration/stage-2-event-store-definitions.md; R-Co src/design/event_store.md (invariants 1-12 at 274-296, DB-tables-per-operation 300-339, Concurrency design 343-376, Open Question #1 451-460); R-Co migrations 001/003/012/013/027/028/1147 and src/event_store/store.zig + platform.zig; lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md plus the SHIPPED lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex, priv/repo/migrations/20260816090045_create_tenant_schemas.exs and test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex; and Ecto/ecto_sql source under deps/ (migrator.ex, migration.ex, postgres/connection.ex, ecto/enum.ex) for every mechanism claim. Section 3 specifies all six tables at field level -- events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, event_payload_store, event_idempotency, events_archive -- each with exact table name, every column (name, Ecto migration type, emitted Postgres DB type, null/default), primary key, every index (explicit name, columns, uniqueness, partial predicate), foreign keys, and for each index/column/FK either a citation to R-Co's own SQL or an explicit reason it is deliberately NOT ported. Section 4 gives the migration plan: six files (20260816120001..120006), module names, ordering constraint (event_payload_store after events for its composite FK), exactly where prefix: prefix() goes on create table / create index / references, reversibility, and the information_schema method for demonstrating acceptance criterion 1. Section 5 gives the Ecto.Schema module plan under lib/letflow/event_store/ (six modules, table<->module mapping, @primary_key/@schema_prefix/@foreign_key_type settings, full field declaration lists, and every changeset signature with cast/validate/constraint contents) plus a normative table of the functions that will deliberately NOT exist (no update_changeset/2 on Event, ArchivedEvent, IdempotencyRecord, StoredPayload, InstanceSequence; no generic changeset/2 on the event schemas; update_changeset/2 exists ONLY on InstanceProjection, per 0003 Decision C point 3). Section 7 quotes verbatim the moduledoc text acceptance criteria 3, 4 and 5 require, so the validator can check it literally. Section 6 lists 13 numbered invariants; section 8 lists cross-module dependencies in both directions; section 9 lists seven open questions explicitly (none silently resolved); section 10 records four verified contradictions between R-Co's event_store.md design doc and R-Co's actual source; section 11 is a two-part traceability table mapping all five acceptance criteria AND every clause of REQ-023's description to a concrete design element. Judgment calls REQ-023 left open were DECIDED with cited rationale, not deferred: sidecar table named event_idempotency (not plat_event_idempotency) because R-Co's own par-01-monthly-range-partitioning.md:203-209 documents the plat_ prefix as denoting a cross-tenant table and flags this table as an exception to that convention, while 0003:304-309 makes Letflow's sidecar unambiguously per-tenant; payload columns jsonb (not text/bytea) matching R-Co 001:28/012:19/1147:125,219; global_seq allocated via Ecto's :bigserial column type, which puts the owning sequence inside the tenant schema automatically and removes the last need for execute/2 raw SQL in these migrations, versus R-Co's explicitly named events_global_seq (divergence stated). tenant_id is carried on events, events_archive and instance_projections per 0003 Decision B's 'tables the adp-0x docs describe' plus R-Co 027:4-10 and 028:18-19, with no DEFAULT (Letflow has no reserved default-tenant UUID, per req022 design 313-324). One verified defect in REQ-022's shipped mechanism was found and resolved inside this design (section 2.4 + 5.2): tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returns {version, module} tuples, but Ecto.Migrator's load_migration!/1 requires Code.ensure_loaded?(module) (migrator.ex:725-731, 744-746) and priv/repo/migrations/*.exs is NOT compiled (mix.exs:20-21 sets elixirc_paths to ["lib"]), so replay_migrations/2 would raise Ecto.MigrationError -- masked today only because mix.exs:48's test alias runs ecto.migrate in the same VM, which Code.compile_file's the modules, and only when they are still pending. The design resolves this with an explicit Code.require_file guard inside tenant_scoped_migrations/0, keeping both shipped @specs byte-identical, and records the rejected directory-source alternative.

issues.description: event_retention_policies has no owning requirement. REQ-026's archive/1 is specified to consult it (docs/requirements.yaml:1126) and R-Co's src/design/event_store.md:327 lists it as a table the archive operation reads (R-Co creates it at migrations/003_event_archive.sql:35-52 and still writes it from store.zig:1240's upsertRetentionPolicy). REQ-023's scope is exactly six tables and this is not one of them; grepping docs/requirements.yaml for 'retention' returns only REQ-026's own lines 1125-1127. No requirement creates this table. This design deliberately does NOT create it (that would silently expand REQ-023's acceptance-criteria-bounded scope). Needs resolution before REQ-026 starts: either extend REQ-026's scope or file a new requirement. Recorded as OQ-1 in section 9 of the artefact.

R-Co's Store.archive() no longer exists -- src/event_store/store.zig:1287-1310 states it was REMOVED under PAR-03 ('No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point'), superseded by whole-partition DETACH/ATTACH/DROP in src/scheduler/partition_retention.zig. R-Co's src/design/event_store.md:115-119 and invariants 11-12 (294-296) still document it as live. Consequence for REQ-026: it ports a function with no current upstream reference implementation, only event_store.md's prose. Consequence for REQ-023, resolved here: R-Co's ON DELETE CASCADE on event_payload_store (012:18, 1147:222) is no longer evidence about archival behaviour, and under CASCADE REQ-026's archive would silently destroy the side-table payload of every archived large event, contradicting 003_event_archive.sql:6-7 and event_store.md:286. This design therefore uses on_delete: :restrict so the gap fails loudly instead of losing tenant data, and flags the resolution itself as OQ-2 for REQ-026.

Gap in REQ-022's shipped design (lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md sections 3.4 and 4): it mandates that every tenant-scoped migration append a {version, ModuleName} tuple to Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0, but did not account for priv/repo/migrations/*.exs never being compiled into the application (mix.exs:20-21 sets elixirc_paths to ["lib"]). Ecto.Migrator.load_migration!/1 requires Code.ensure_loaded?(module) to be true for an atom source (deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migrator.ex:725-731, 744-746), so replay_migrations/2 would raise Ecto.MigrationError for any tenant whose schema still has those versions pending, in any VM where mix ecto.migrate did not itself just compile them. It is masked in mix test only because mix.exs:48's test alias runs ecto.migrate in-process and because only pending migrations are ever loaded (migrator.ex:647-658) -- i.e. it would pass on a fresh test DB and fail on a warm one. Resolved inside REQ-023's design (sections 2.4 and 5.2) via a Code.require_file guard in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 that leaves both shipped @specs unchanged; flagged here so REQ-022's design doc gets corrected at the source.

R-Co's src/design/event_store.md contains three further statements contradicted by R-Co's own shipped source, all documented in section 10 of the artefact so downstream requirements do not port stale guidance: (C-2) invariants 4 and 5 plus Open Question #1 (lines 280, 282, 451-460) describe a uq_event_idempotency index on events plus a two-phase events-then-events_archive check, both of which migrations/1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql:162-165 and :192-193 removed in favour of the sidecar table -- this is exactly the supersession 0003 Decision C 2(b) already recorded, so it is resolved by existing Letflow decision rather than newly decided; (C-3) event_payload_store.created_at means the side-table row's own insert time at 012_event_retention.sql:21 but the referenced event's created_at at 1147:218/store.zig:843-849, a silent same-name meaning swap -- this design splits the two into event_created_at and inserted_at, matching the unambiguous name R-Co itself used on webhook_deliveries at 1147:250; (C-4) event_store.md:440 and 012:18 give event_payload_store.event_id a single-column UNIQUE index while 1147:221 replaced it with a composite one -- this design keeps the single-column form, which is strictly stronger and matches REQ-023's own wording at requirements.yaml:933. Additionally event_store.md:4 lists only two files for src/event_store/ where three exist (platform.zig); Letflow's own docs/migration/stage-2-event-store-definitions.md:7 already carries the corrected count of 3, so only R-Co's header is stale.
